Where can i get very old (but still functional) laptops for free? (Maybe a recycling center?)
I am going to take them out of the case, clean them, and try and put them back together... Good practice... may also flat-mount one or two on plywood over in /v/diy

I doubt you can get them for free, by companies that lease or rent laptops often have auctions on the old laptops or sell them very cheap.

The problem with most old laptops is that the battery is dead or the power inverter doesn't work anymore. It basically makes a dead laptop. Replacing a power inverter is very hard work, finding a new battery when they don't even make that battery anymore is going to be difficult if not expensive.

Recycling centers just smash old computers and laptops and recycle the metals and materials in them.

You might go looking for schools and old businesses and asking if they have any old laptops they are not using that they might have in storage or something.
School districts also often hold auctions, which can be a great source for old hardware. Back in 2006 or 2007 I picked up two PowerMac G4s for $5 a piece that way.

Other then the power issue, laptop screens don't have the longest lifespan ever. Even less so with the older makes, I should imagine. And the costs and effort required to repair these things isn't really worth it.
You can also check the dump. I once found four ~4 year old dell monitors that had some sort of paint on the screens. I cleaned them off and sold them for ~$100 each.

Look at distribution centers for your local thrift/second hand stores. I go into Boise to the Idaho Youth Ranch center and you can buy thrift store stuff by the pound but they also have a dedicated PC area full of peripherals, cards, desktops and laptops. Found some great pieces for people just wanting to get online and alot of stuff that would be good for some DIY/power efficient projects.

Just stay away from p4 and beyond. Shit like that eats up power like noones business. Get a Rasp Pi or Arduino or whatever for that stuff.

The laptop I'm currently using to write this was picked out of a recycling centre. I was astonished to boot it up and find that it's a later Core2Duo, 500gb HD, high resolution display.. just had a bad RAM stick and this Vista thing that was just.. :| Now running Xubuntu 14.04, and even without the extra 2gb of memory, fun as heck and cool to boot..
